quotes.text: When a machine handles the triage, enrichment, and correlation, speed becomes cheap. What becomes expensive is accuracy. What becomes precious is the human time spent on the stuff that actually matters.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures how agentic triage shifts the economics of security operations.

quotes.text: If an agent can disable user accounts, it's a system administrator. If an agent can isolate endpoints from your network, it's a security operator.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for governing agents as privileged identities rather than tools.

quotes.text: Complexity is not solved by adding intelligence to one place. It is solved by distributing intelligence across specialized agents and letting them validate each other.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the multi-agent design principle behind reliable agentic defense.

quotes.text: The bottleneck in modern security isn't finding problems. It's validating which problems matter. An organization drowning in alerts isn't drowning because detection is failing. It's drowning because validation is missing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes alert fatigue as a validation problem rather than a detection problem.

chapters.title: The metrics trap: MTTR vs. outcomes
Governing agents and the autonomy spectrum
Phased implementation and the agent fabric

takeaways: Alert fatigue is a system design problem: agents should become the orchestration layer so humans supervise decisions instead of clicking through every alert.
Dwell time and true positives are better SOC metrics than MTTR, and multi-agent validation cuts false positives more than bigger models do.
Agents need their own identities, least privilege, guardrails, audit trails and a phased rollout from assistive to semi-autonomous before they gain more autonomy.
hook: SOC analysts drown in alerts while MTTR dashboards look great and attackers stay hidden. This episode is for security leaders and architects who want to move from human middleware to a governed security agent fabric, with phishing triage, conditional access and multi-agent validation as concrete examples.
